stories.headline: Don’t stand in the way of protesting students, they are voice of India: Rahul tells PM and HM
stories.deck: LoP Rahul Gandhi made these remarks after interacting with students, including activists of the party’s students’ wing, National Students’ Union of India (NSUI), who were injured during recent protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the weekend
stories.bodyText:
Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Wednesday (October 14, 2026) asked Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah not to stand in the way of protesting students, describing them as the voice of India.
Mr. Gandhi made the remarks after he met students, including activists of the party’s students’ wing, the National Students’ Union of India (NSUI), who were injured during recent protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
The meeting happened at the 10, Janpath residence of Congress Parliamentary Party chairperson Sonia Gandhi.
‘No Hindu, no Muslim’
The Opposition leader asked the students to introduce themselves, narrate their ordeal after Delhi Police personnel picked them up from the protesting sites, and then, urged the students to form a human chain by holding each others hands.
“Amit Shah ji, look at this properly. Here there is no Hindu, no Muslim, no caste, no gender. There is one voice, one protest — it is the voice of Hindustan,” he said.
“And you are standing in front of this voice and the Prime Minister ji is standing in front of this voice. I give you a suggestion — do not stand in front of this voice. No one can stand in front of this voice,” Mr. Gandhi added.
Inhuman treatment: students
During the interaction, some students recounted what they described as inhuman treatment in police custody, alleging that they were beaten, abused and hit in their private parts.
Mr. Gandhi described the students as the party’s shers and shernis (lions and lionesses) and assured them that the Congress would stand by them. He said those responsible for alleged police excesses would be held accountable, from the Prime Minister and Home Minister Amit Shah to the police constables involved in the incidents.
‘Preserve evidence’
The Congress leader also urged the students to preserve video and photographic evidence of how they are being treated in custody.
“Peaceful protest is your right. We will not allow anyone to snatch it away,” Mr. Gandhi said in a post on X, adding that the day would come when those seeking to silence democracy would face the law.
The interaction also addressed a concern within the party that while Mr. Gandhi has showcased student protesters such as Neha Bora, several NSUI and Youth Congress activists have not received similar visibility.

stories.headline: Keralam-born Nithya Raman leads in Los Angeles mayoral race
stories.bodyText: Washington: Keralam-born Nithya Raman is maintaining a lead over her former political ally and incumbent Mayor Karen Bass in the Los Angeles mayoral race after a fiery televised pre-poll debate. . Bass (73) and Raman (45) – both Democrats – sparred in the debate on Tuesday night over issues such as the homelessness crisis, police department leadership, and public safety in Los Angeles, the second-largest city in the US. . If elected in the November 3 polls, Raman will be the first Indian-American Mayor of Los Angeles. .NBC local news helicopter crashes in Los Angeles, killing three. A member of the Democratic Socialist movement, Raman has served for six years as a City Councilmember. . Raman, who had endorsed Bass for re-election before deciding to enter the fray, accused her of being a “missing-in-action” mayor for her absence when the city battled a massive fire in January last year. . Bass was on the offensive in the hour-long debate and accused Raman of being “unserious, indecisive” and not ready for the top city job. . Raman hit back, saying that Los Angeles “cannot afford another four years of decline, mismanagement, or excuses.” . “Are you better off today than you were four years ago?” Raman asked the viewers, quoting the famous line of President Ronald Regan in the presidential election debate in 1980. . Born in Kerala on July 28, 1981, Raman moved to Louisiana when she was six. She earned a bachelor's degree in political theory from Harvard University and then a master's degree in urban planning from MIT. . Ahead of the Tuesday night debate, Raman led by 11 points over Bass in the survey conducted by Berkeley’s Institute of Governmental Studies, University of California, and co-sponsored by the Los Angeles Times. . The survey, conducted between September 15 and 20, found 39 per cent of voters favouring Raman for the Los Angeles Mayor post, compared with 28 per cent for Bass. Whereas almost one-third of the surveyed voters were undecided. . On Wednesday, a day after the debate, prediction market Kalshi put Raman’s odds of winning in the mayoral election at 56 per cent, compared with 45 per cent for Bass. . Citing rising homelessness in Los Angeles “despite hundreds of millions of dollars spent”, Raman said a vote for her would help build a “city that’s functional, that’s affordable and where people are welcomed here to build their dreams once again.” . Stepping up her attack on Bass for her absence during the massive fire at Palisades in South California last January, Raman said she was in the city’s emergency operations centre attending to the needs of evacuated constituents throughout the disaster. . “The question I heard over and over, there and across the entire city, was, ‘Where is our mayor? Where is our mayor?’” Raman said. . “You will not have to ask where our mayor is if I am mayor. I will be on the front lines,” Raman asserted.

stories.headline: Samson joins Rohit, Kohli in elite T20I club after quick 50 vs West Indies
stories.deck: Sanju Samson has made waves in the cricketing world by smashing his 100th six in T20 Internationals. This achievement came during a thrilling fourth T20I match against the West Indies, where he scored an impressive 56 runs off just 23 deliveries. Leading Indian cricketers in sixes, he showcases his stellar talent, having accumulated 687 runs in just 24 games in 2026.
stories.bodyText:
Sanju Samson added another milestone to his T20I career on Wednesday, becoming only the sixth Indian batter to hit 100 sixes in the format during the fourth T20I against West Indies at Hyderabad's Rajiv Gandhi International Stadium. The wicketkeeper-batter reached the landmark in style while launching India's pursuit of a daunting 248-run target, producing an explosive 56 off just 23 deliveries.
Samson's aggressive innings featured six fours and four sixes at a strike rate of 243.48, giving India early momentum after West Indies captain Shai Hope struck an unbeaten century to power the visitors to 247/3. However, Samson's counterattack ended when Keemo Paul dismissed him for 56, with Shimron Hetmyer completing a catch near the boundary.
Samson joins India's elite six-hitting club
With 102 sixes to his name in T20Is, Samson has joined an exclusive group of Indian batters to have crossed the 100-six mark. Rohit Sharma leads the list with 205 sixes, followed by Suryakumar Yadav with 179.
Abhishek Sharma, who had 141 sixes at the time of filing, is third on the list, while Hardik Pandya and Virat Kohli have struck 126 and 124 sixes, respectively.
A productive year for Samson
The milestone comes amid a productive year for the Kerala-born batter. 
Samson has scored 687 runs in 24 matches and innings in 2026, averaging 29.86 at a strike rate of 178.44. His tally includes seven half-centuries, with a highest score of 97 not out.
One of the defining phases of his year came during the ICC Men's T20 World Cup, when Samson registered three consecutive half-centuries, beginning with a Super Eight clash against West Indies and continuing through the final against New Zealand. His performances earned him the Player of the Tournament award and helped India secure their third T20 World Cup title.
Samson's overall T20I record
In 76 T20Is and 68 innings, Samson has accumulated 1,719 runs at an average of 27.28 and a strike rate of 158.87. His international record includes three centuries and 10 half-centuries.

stories.headline: ISCR, CHAKRA sign MoU to boost clinical research in Maharashtra
stories.bodyText: Mumbai: The Indian Society for Clinical Research (ISCR) and the Centre for Health Applied Knowledge & Research Autonomy (CHAKRA) have signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to strengthen responsible, ethical and high-quality clinical research capacity across Maharashtra. According to Built on Scale, Turning to Science, a July 2026 report by BCG and HealthKois, India’s life sciences innovation ecosystem is gaining momentum, with more than 10 novel drug assets originating in India over the past decade and the innovation pipeline expanding by around 1.5 times. However, India’s participation in clinical research remains relatively low compared with its population and disease burden. The BCG–HealthKois report notes that India accounts for about 15 per cent of the global disease burden but conducts around 4 per cent of global clinical trials. Separately, ICME INTENT reported that India accounts for 18 per cent of the world’s population but just 1.4 per cent of global clinical research. .CDSCO cancels 7 ethics committees for non-compliance with clinical trial rules. Under the MoU, ISCR and CHAKRA will work together to strengthen clinical research capabilities at the site and institutional levels. The collaboration will focus on Good Clinical Practice (GCP) and ethics training, research governance, standard operating procedures and quality frameworks, as well as site readiness and capability mapping across CHAKRA’s hub-and-spoke network. The partnership will also support academic and professional development and facilitate knowledge exchange to promote globally benchmarked clinical research practices across Maharashtra. Commenting on the partnership, ISCR President Dr Seema Pai said, “Only one in 5,000 to 10,000 molecules tested in the laboratory progresses to human studies, underscoring the importance of ensuring that the sites carrying this science forward are built on equally rigorous foundations. Our collaboration with CHAKRA brings together ISCR’s expertise in training, ethics and quality with CHAKRA’s network to strengthen the readiness of research sites across Maharashtra to conduct high-quality, globally benchmarked studies. We look forward to building this capacity together.” CHAKRA CEO Dr Ranjana Kumar said, “Strengthening research capacity at the grassroots is central to CHAKRA’s mission. Partnering with ISCR will help our hub-and-spoke network build the skills, governance frameworks and site readiness needed to participate in ethical, high-quality clinical research. Ultimately, stronger research capabilities can benefit researchers, institutions, patients and the communities we serve.”

briefs.headline: Hold panchayat polls in U.P. within 3 months: HC to State poll body
briefs.deck: The petitioner had moved the court seeking direction to the poll body to place on record a detailed time-bound schedule for completion of the entire panchayat election process well before the expiry of the district panchayat tenure
briefs.bodyText:
The Allahabad High Court on Wednesday (October 14, 2026) directed the Uttar Pradesh State Election Commission to hold polls to Panchayati Raj institutions in Uttar Pradesh within three months.
The order was passed by a Bench comprising Justices Ajit Kumar and Garima Prashad while allowing the plea by Dashrath Yadav and others.
The petitioner had moved the court seeking direction to the poll body to place on record a detailed time-bound schedule for completion of the entire panchayat election process well before the expiry of the district panchayat tenure.
These three-tier polls are called so that elections to zila panchayats (district level), Kshetra panchayat (intermediary) and Gram Panchayat (village level) are held simultaneously.
The Bench observed, "The State Government and the State Election Commission shall proceed forthwith with the preparatory steps, issue the election programme, and complete the elections to the village panchayats in Uttar Pradesh within three months from the date of this judgement. The schedule shall provide for the steps necessary to constitute the elected bodies within the above-prescribed period."
The court said, "The State Government and the State Election Commission shall conduct the entire elections under the existing reservation arrangement, including 27% reservation for Other Backward Classes.”
"The elections shall not be conducted by treating the OBC-reserved seats as open seats merely because the Dedicated Commission's inquiry remains pending. Reservations for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and women shall be maintained in accordance with the applicable laws, subject to the aggregate ceiling governing vertical reservation," the court said.
"The State Government shall provide the staff, funds, security and other logistical assistance as may be required by the State Election Commission to hold elections within the time bound period above. The time allowed for completion of the elections does not extend an administrator's tenure beyond the period permitted by law. Any intervening administrative arrangement must remain within the applicable statutory limits," added the court.
The court further said, "The dedicated Commission shall continue with its investigation and inquiry considering the observations contained in the body of the judgment for collective empirical data qua OBC and preparation of report on that basis.
"It shall complete its process within the period already prescribed within such extended period as be provided by the State Government. The State shall thereafter examine the recommendations and undertake the statutory steps and amendments, where required, for their lawful implementation."
"The relief for quashing the Government order dated May 25, 2026 invoking power under Section 12(3-A) for appointment of administrator and so also relief for quashing of the appointments of outgoing Pradhans as administrators of respective Gram Panchayats are hereby rejected. The relief for declaration with regard to Sections 12(3-A) and 12-BB(3) as ultra vires Article 243-E is also hereby rejected and hence the Writ petitions in that regard stand rejected," the court said.

briefs.headline: Ankita Bhandari murder: Parents detained during India Gate protest, released around 5 am on Oct 15
Jantar Mantar breach: Das, Ranka sent to 5-day custody
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: CJP members 
Saurav Das
 and Ashutosh Ranka have been sent to five days of judicial custody, while Ajinkya Shinde has been bound down, after 14 party members allegedly trespassed into Jantar Mantar, which is no longer a designated protest venue, and obstructed cops on duty. Bound down means an individual has to appear before an IO whenever called and inform cops before leaving the city.
Police said the action was prompted by repeated alleged violations of law and concerns that accused could again disturb public peace.
‘Concerns they were likely to breach peace’
Police also feared that they could instigate others. Two FIRs have been registered, including one under the section relating to criminal conspiracy.
DCP (New Delhi) Sachin Sharma said, “Police personnel deployed at the spot intervened and attempted to stop them. However, the protesters allegedly obstructed police personnel in the discharge of their official duties.” Subsequently, all the persons were bound down in the respective case as per law.
The DCP said that in view of their alleged repeated attempts to disturb peace and violate the law, Ranka, Das, and Shinde were arrested under relevant preventive provisions. 
“Their alleged attempts to instigate others via social media to engage in similar unlawful activities were also taken into consideration,” he added.
The three were produced before the special executive magistrate, where proceedings under Sections 126 (security for keeping peace in other cases) and 170 (arrest to prevent commission of cognisable offences) of the BNSS were initiated. Police also submitted videos of CJP representatives jumping a gate and unfurling the flag at Jantar Mantar Tuesday. The court, considering the kalandra (preventive legal measure) details, in view of their repeated violations of law and serious apprehension that if released on bail, they will again violate law and instigate others, remanded Das and Ranka to five days of judicial custody. Special executive magistrate Mahesh Kumar Meena held that their conduct after being released earlier after executing personal and surety bonds of Rs 50,000 each for maintaining peace and good behaviour showed they were likely to breach “peace and tranquillity”. The magistrate had directed them to “keep peace in the area for a period of one year from the date of order”. Their lawyer, Abhisht Hela, argued that an executive magistrate had no power to order judicial custody and said he would approach Delhi High Court.

Shinde was released on personal bond and surety of Rs 5,000. However, he was “bound down to maintain peace and good behaviour for six months”. Under Section 141 of BNSS, a magistrate can order the arrest and detention of a person found to have breached a peace bond executed under Section 136 for the remainder of the bond period. The matter has been listed for further inquiry on Oct 19.
The FIR invokes sections 223, which deals with disobedience of an order duly promulgated by a public servant, 332 (house-trespass in order to commit an offence) and 61 (2) (criminal conspiracy) of BNS at Connaught Place police station.
The second FIR was registered under sections 221 (obstructing public servant in discharge of his public functions), 115 (voluntarily causing hurt), 132 (assault or criminal force to deter public servant from discharge of his duty), 121 (voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt to deter public servant from his duty) and 3 (5) (common intention) of BNS at Parliament Street police station.

briefs.headline: 'It was suicide, not murder': Model breaks silence in UP bizman's death case
briefs.deck: Shraddha Dubey posted a video denying involvement in the death of restaurant owner Shiva Sharma. She claims that Sharma's death resulted from suicide rather than murder. Dubey expressed her willingness to cooperate with police and deny absconding. Sharma's mother accused Dubey and others of murder following Sharma's fall from the apartment. Investigators are currently examining the allegations…
briefs.bodyText:
LUCKNOW: A day after being named as the prime accused in the death of 28-year-old restaurant owner 
Shiva Sharma
, model and social media influencer Shraddha Dubey surfaced in a video posted on social media, denying any wrongdoing and claiming that Sharma’s death was a case of suicide, not murder.
She also urged the media to stop linking her to politicians and senior officials and said she was willing to appear before the police and record her statement.
The 1-minute-15-second video emerged even as Lucknow Police intensified efforts to trace the accused. On Tuesday, police announced a reward of Rs 25,000 each for information leading to the arrest of Dubey, her sister Rashmi Dubey and Tanveer Ali alias Danish in connection with the case.
In the video, Dubey alleged that rumours were being spread about her and objected to what she described as attempts to link her to politicians and bureaucrats based on social media associations.
“Just because someone follows me or is connected to me on Instagram does not mean I know them or have any relationship with them,” she said, appealing to the media not to draw conclusions without evidence.
Dubey also denied that she was absconding and claimed she intended to cooperate with investigators.
“I am not missing. I want to come before the police and tell them everything I know. I want to place the complete truth before them,” she said.
Dubey asserted that Sharma’s death was not a murder. “The truth is that Shiva Sharma did not die due to murder but by suicide,” she said, adding that she was currently not in a condition to explain the circumstances in detail because of her health.
Sharma died on October 9 after falling from the fourth floor of Awadh Green Apartment in Hazratganj. According to police sources, he had been in a relationship with Dubey for around four months.
Following the incident, Sharma’s mother, Ranjana Sharma, lodged an FIR accusing Dubey, her sister Rashmi, driver Adil and others of murdering her son. The family has alleged that Dubey pushed Sharma from the building, a claim that investigators are examining.
All those named in the FIR remain untraceable. In a recent development, an SUV allegedly linked to Dubey was found abandoned near the India-Nepal border in Bahraich district.

briefs.headline: Commercial ship catches fire in Romanian waters in latest Black Sea incident
briefs.deck: The attacks have highlighted the growing threat that drone warfare linked to the Russia-Ukraine war poses ‌to commercial shipping in the Black Sea
briefs.bodyText:
A commercial ship anchored in Romanian territorial waters caught fire late on Wednesday (October 14, 2026) and the crew evacuated, Romanian authorities said, the latest in a series of incidents in the Black Sea underlying shipping risks near NATO's eastern flank.
Five commercial ships have been hit in the Black Sea off the coasts of NATO members Romania and Bulgaria since early October, with about 23 sailors dead or missing.
The attacks have highlighted the growing threat that drone warfare linked to the Russia-Ukraine war poses to commercial shipping in the Black Sea.
Romania's naval authority said on Wednesday (October 14, 2026) it was notified by the Comoros-flagged chemical and oil tanker Yara J of a fire onboard. The crew was safe and had evacuated, it added.
Defence Minister Radu Miruta said it was unclear whether the ship had been hit by a drone and an investigation was pending.
The ship was anchored about 8 to 10 nautical miles (14.8 to 18.52 km) southeast of the Sulina canal, inside Romanian territorial waters.
The river Danube's Sulina Canal is a key route for Ukrainian grain exports and delays caused by bad weather and insufficient staffing have created a backlog of dozens of ships waiting to cross it.
Russia has been bombing Ukraine's Black Sea ports, forcing Kyiv to rely increasingly on Danube river ports and shipping routes close to the coasts of NATO members Bulgaria and Romania.
Multiple drones breached Romanian airspace on Wednesday (October 14, 2026) near its border with Ukraine. Mr. Miruta said radar systems did not show a drone headed for the ship.
NATO member Romania shares a 614-km (381-mile) land border with Ukraine and has reported repeated breaches of its airspace by Russian drones over the past four years, as well as mines floating in the Black Sea across key trade and energy routes.
"These drone attacks are direct consequences of Russia’s war of aggression against Ukraine and endanger not only shipping in our region but also vital agricultural supplies to other continents," Romanian President Nicusor Dan said on Wednesday (October 14, 2026) after a call with neighbouring Bulgaria's president.
"We agreed that Romania and Bulgaria will work closely together to push for stronger counter-drone measures within the EU and NATO."

briefs.headline: Weeks after judicial panel held him responsible for Indore water tragedy, IAS officer made Collector
briefs.deck: Slamming the fresh appointment, Mr. Patwari questioned whether the action taken by the government was based on the panel’s report and whether facts were considered before appointing Mr. Sisonia as a District Collector
briefs.bodyText:
Just weeks after a Judicial Commission probe report on the Indore water contamination deaths was submitted to the Madhya Pradesh High Court, IAS officer Rohit Sisonia — the then-Additional Commissioner (water supply) of Indore Municipal Corporation, who was one of the two officials held “primarily responsible” for the tragedy — has been appointed Collector of Raisen district in a bureaucratic shuffle by the Government.
The appointment has been criticised by the Opposition Congress, with State unit president Jitu Patwari raising questions over the transparency of transfer postings in the State. “Instead of accountability, favouritism is being prioritized in important postings,” he wrote on X.
Mr. Sisonia, an IAS officer of 2017 batch, was posted as a Deputy Secretary in the Farmers Welfare and Agriculture Development Department. He has been made Raisen Collector in the reshuffle announced late on October 13, in which 23 IAS officers have been transferred.
After the tragedy in Indore’s Bhagirathpura had come to light in December 2025, Mr. Sisonia was among the officials who were suspended for negligence by Chief Minister Mohan Yadav on January 2, 2026.
The one-member judicial panel of retired High Court judge Justice Sushil Kumar Gupta, formed to probe the reasons of the tragedy, submitted its report dated August 18 to the Indore Bench of the High Court in September. The report blamed mixing of sewage water with drinking water — due to parallel laying of two pipelines that had been damaged over the years — for the bacterial contamination of water that led to more than 30 deaths in the area.
The report held Mr. Sisonia and the then-executive engineer (water supply) Sanjeev Shrivastava “primary responsible” for for various lapses in inspections, carrying out repair works, and several delays in projects to replace the water pipeline which further led to the tragedy.
Slamming the fresh appointment, Mr. Patwari questioned whether the action taken by the government was based on the panel’s report and whether facts were considered before appointing Mr. Sisonia as a District Collector.
“36 people died in the tragedy of contaminated water in Bhagirathpura, Indore — India’s first Water Plus City! After this criminal incident, the administrative officer Rohit Sisodiya, who was removed, has been made the Raisen Collector by the Mohan Yadav’s government,” he wrote.
“The victim families of Bhagirathpura are still awaiting justice and action against the culprits today. The BJP government should first explain what action has been taken on the inquiry commission’s report and on what facts were considered before appointing the concerned officer as Collector?” Mr. Patwari said, while questioning the transparency of transfer posting in the State.
“Has the transfer industry now turned into a transfer factory? Instead of accountability, favouritism is being prioritized in important postings! Allegations of corruption/commission are also coming to light as evidence!” Mr. Patwari said.

stories.headline: Karnataka police to probe sting operation; 2 minors among 5 under lens
stories.deck: Karnataka home minister Priyank Kharge stated that state police are capable of handling the sting operation investigation. Following his statement, five individuals were questioned by police regarding the matter. Two minors remain under interrogation, while three others were released after questioning. Former CM Siddaramaiah has filed a complaint alleging a conspiracy to damage his reputation.…
stories.bodyText:
BENGALURU: Hours after Karnataka home minister Priyank Kharge Wednesday said state police were "capable" of investigating an alleged sting operation targeting former CM Siddaramaiah, city police picked up and questioned five people, including a JD(S) worker and two minors, in the case.
While three were allowed to go after questioning, the two minors are still under interrogation, police sources said, adding the alleged suspects were identified based on IP address.
The minister ruled out a CBI probe, a demand of Union minister HD Kumaraswamy. "Why is a CBI inquiry needed in this case? What is the cause of action? This is also part of a conspiracy to tarnish Siddaramaiah's reputation," he said. The central probe agency was yet to complete 2-3 cases entrusted to it and was seeking personnel from the state to expedite investigations, he added.
Cops took JD(S) member without case: HDK Siddaramaiah had lodged a complaint with the police commissioner, alleging a conspiracy to damage his reputation through false information.
CCB cybercrime police began monitoring social-media platforms and tracing IP addresses of accounts that circulated the videos.
Kumaraswamy accused Congress govt of targeting JD(S) social-media workers instead of pursuing those allegedly behind the sting operation. However, he, in a social-media statement Wednesday, claimed police had taken away Shankar, a member of JD(S) social media team, without filing a case.

stories.headline: Karnataka police reopen 2012 case against surrendered Maoist as rehabilitation promises remain unfulfilled
stories.deck: The development comes amid reports that Kotehonda Ravindra, one of the surrendered Maoists, has gone on a hunger strike in a Keralam prison despite having fallen ‘seriously ill’.
stories.bodyText:
The Karnataka police have reopened a 2012 case in Sakleshpur’s Yeslur against a surrendered Maoist, while preparations are under way to reopen another case in Dakshina Kannada against four others, even as the surrendered Maoists are hoping for an early release from prison.
The development comes amid reports that Kotehonda Ravindra, one of the surrendered Maoists, has gone on a hunger strike in a Keralam prison despite having fallen “seriously ill”. Meanwhile, members of the Naxal Surrender and Rehabilitation Committee allege that the State government is yet to honour its commitments to the Maoists made during their surrender.
Exchange of fire
A senior police officer said the reopened case pertains to an alleged exchange of gunfire between the Anti-Naxal Force (ANF) and the Maoists in 2012 near Sakleshpur. Slain Maoist leader Vikram Gowda and Ravindra have been named as accused in the case.
“The Maoists had visited a village to collect rations from a house when the ANF was conducting a combing operation, leading to an exchange of fire. There were no injuries,” he told The Hindu.
When asked why the case had been reopened now, the officer said that the police had no leads at the time, but the surrender of the Maoists had them reopen it. “Ravindra was taken into our custody for a few days, but he did not reveal anything. However, a witness has identified him,” he told The Hindu.
Meanwhile, Khalandar Koila, the Special Public Prosecutor (SPP) appointed by the government to handle cases against Maoists, confirmed to The Hindu that another case involving four accused is being reopened in Subramanya, Dakshina Kannada.
“We have only two NIA cases left now after ensuring that many cases have resulted in acquittals. But now, they are reopening cases that had already been closed by submitting a C-report,” he said.
No response
Meanwhile, K.P. Sreepal, a member of the rehabilitation committee set up by the government, alleged that the State government had barely fulfilled the commitments made to the Maoists during their surrender.
“We have got most cases cleared. However, Keralam has filed a heap of cases, which are yet to even go to trial,” he said.
He stressed that one of the key promises made by the government was to ensure that the Maoists were not left to rot in prison.
Mr. Sreepal listed the alleged unfulfilled promises, saying that no fast-track courts had been set up after a court rejected the proposal, citing a technical issue. “No effort was made by the government after that. Although they appointed SPPs, the government did not pay their salaries, which led to the resignation of one of them,” he alleged.
Remaining cases
According to the data, about 41 cases are pending in Kundapur, five each in Shivamogga and Sringeri, three in Karkala, and two in Bengaluru. In addition, more than 100 cases are pending in Keralam.
Mr. Sreepal further noted that the government had promised to coordinate with the Keralam government and try to resolve the cases, but no in-person meeting had been held to discuss the matter. “Now, even reaching the officials has become a difficult task,” he said.

stories.headline: Three factory workers sustain injuries in boiler blast in Bengaluru

Bengaluru

stories.headline: BMRCL begins soil testing on Sarjapur Road for proposed Namma Metro Red Line corridor
stories.deck: The investigation will assess the characteristics of the soil and underlying rock formations along the proposed alignment before construction work begins.
stories.bodyText:
The Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited (BMRCL) has begun geotechnical investigations along Sarjapur Road for the proposed 37.8-km Bengaluru Metro Phase 3A corridor, also known as the Red Line, which is planned to connect Sarjapur in southeast Bengaluru with Hebbal in the north.
The investigation will assess the characteristics of the soil and underlying rock formations along the proposed alignment before construction work begins. The findings will help engineers evaluate ground conditions and determine the technical requirements for building the elevated and underground sections of the metro corridor, according to the BMRCL officials.
Speaking to The Hindu, a senior BMRCL official said, “The study will provide essential information about soil stability, geological formations and other ground conditions along the route. These findings will guide decisions on foundation depth, structural design and the construction requirements for metro pillars, helping ensure the safety and stability of the infrastructure.”
Meanwhile, the proposed project awaits approval from the Union government, the officials confirmed. The State government has submitted the Detailed Project Report (DPR) for the corridor, but the Centre has not specified a timeline for granting its approval.
As previously reported by The Hindu, the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) informed Parliament in August that the project was still undergoing detailed scrutiny. Its approval would depend on the outcome of the feasibility assessment and the availability of financial resources.
The clarification was provided in a written reply to a question raised by Ajay Maken in the Rajya Sabha. The ministry stated that metro rail projects require substantial capital investment and must undergo a comprehensive assessment in accordance with the Metro Rail Policy, 2017, before receiving approval. Consequently, it said that no specific timeline could be provided for sanctioning the proposed corridor.
The project has been under review for an extended period, with discussions between the State and Union governments focusing on its estimated cost, particularly the expenditure associated with underground construction.
In response to concerns raised during the appraisal process, the BMRCL undertook a cost-reduction exercise involving changes to underground station designs, adjustments to the alignment and modifications to station locations. The corporation also engaged an engineering consultancy to examine the project estimates and identify opportunities to reduce expenditure without compromising operational requirements.
According to the BMRCL officials, the revisions included reducing the lengths of underground stations, comparing construction costs with those of similar metro projects and modifying various engineering specifications. These measures substantially lowered the estimated project cost.
Once completed, the Red Line is expected to improve connectivity between Hebbal and Sarjapur Road, linking important residential and commercial areas, including Koramangala and Bengaluru’s Central Business District, as well as the city’s southeastern information technology corridor.

briefs.headline: Beyond Freedom Park: Traders seek more protest sites across Bengaluru
briefs.deck: Traders Push For Decentralisation, Activists Bat For Right To Dissent
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: The demand to move protests beyond Freedom Park is gathering momentum, with activists pushing for the right to hold demonstrations closer to the communities and institutions their grievances concern, while traders are seeking designated venues across Bengaluru to protect commercial activity.
Sajjan Raj Mehta, a trade activist, has written to the chief minister proposing five protest hubs across the city. He said concentrating demonstrations in the central business district (CBD) disrupts traffic and prevents customers and workers from reaching commercial establishments, imposing financial hardship on small merchants, street vendors and transport workers.
Activists say decentralisation must protect the right to dissent rather than simply relocate restrictions.
The letter to the CM proposes zone-wise designated protest hubs in each of GBA’s five divisions, seeking advance public notifications and clear traffic-management protocols for permitted rallies.
Prakash Bhojani, president of Karnataka Hosiery and Garment Association, told 
TOI traders were feeling the impact, particularly during the festive season. The association has 1,500 shops under its establishment.
Kalaram Choudhury, president of Karnataka Stainless Steel Trade and Industry Association, said: “Peaceful protests are the backbone of democracy and must be respected. We request both the Centre and the state govt to provide designated protest venues outside city centres to protect public convenience, traffic, trade, and MSMEs without affecting democratic rights.”
Activists from Campaign for the Right to Protest have urged the govt to withdraw the 2021 police licensing order and restore the 2009 framework. As reported by 
TOI on Oct 14, they have written a letter to Shivakumar and home minister Priyank Kharge, arguing that centralising demonstrations at Freedom Park has restricted marginalised groups’ ability to engage directly with authorities.
They cited protests by workers, farmers, Dalit activists and residents over local civic issues, saying demonstrations should take place where grievances can be addressed — outside labour offices, the chief electoral officer’s office or other relevant institutions.
Other activists pointed out that the Karnataka high court’s Aug 2022 order directed compliance with the 2021 licensing regime, and argued that the state govt retains the power to amend or withdraw it. The 2021 order itself allows the police commissioner to designate another suitable venue depending on the situation.
The demand has gathered urgency amid the anti-SIR mobilisation. Activists have called for chief electoral officer (CEO) V Anbukumar’s resignation if he was “unable or unwilling to ensure the cancellation of the Special Intensive Revision in Karnataka, restoration of the electoral rolls as they stood in Jan 2025, and safeguards against arbitrary deletions”. They have also demanded a transparent, publicly accountable process for future revisions.

briefs.headline: Bengaluru realtor shoots at business rival
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: Police launched a manhunt for a realtor who escaped after allegedly firing a shot at his business rival. The incident took place near NICE bridge at Pillaganahalli late Wednesday evening, when the suspect, Gottigere Sampangi, allegedly shot at and injured Mental Seena of Weavers’ Colony.
“According to eyewitnesses and other commuters, the two were arguing loudly. At one stage, Sampangi is said to have pulled out his revolver and fired a bullet into Seena’s leg before escaping,” a senior police officer said. However, cops are yet to confirm who shot at Seena. Sampangi is at large.
Seena, undergoing treatment at a hospital, is out of danger, police said. Sampangi and Seena were once friends but developed differences over real estate deals.

briefs.headline: BJP worker killed in Bengaluru as high-end car rams gas tanker near Devanahalli; three injured
briefs.deck: According to the police, when the vehicle reached the highway on the Hoskote–Dabaspet Ring Road stretch, the driver allegedly attempted to overtake a gas tanker ahead of them and rammed into it.
briefs.bodyText:
BJP party worker and realtor Shivakumar, 50, from Malur, was killed and three others were injured after the speeding high-end car they were travelling in rammed a gas tanker near Rani Cross on the Kempegowda International Airport Road in Devanahalli on Tuesday.
The injured have been identified as Chandan, Pradeep and Vinod Kumar. They were shifted to a nearby hospital.
According to the police, Shivakumar and the three injured were travelling from Chitradurga to Malur. When they reached the highway on the Hoskote-Dobbspet Ring Road stretch, the driver allegedly attempted to overtake a gas tanker.
During the manoeuvre, the speeding car rammed the tanker. The impact was severe, leaving the front portion of the luxury vehicle completely mangled. Shivakumar sustained critical injuries and died.
The Devanahalli traffic police have registered a case.

briefs.headline: Karnataka will strengthen finances of local bodies: Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar
briefs.deck: Government to frame guidelines for ‘People’s Plan’; proposes ward-level meetings and GST revenue share for local bodies
briefs.bodyText:
The Karnataka government will take steps to improve the financial position of gram panchayats and strengthen decentralised governance, Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar said on Wednesday (October 14).
Chairing a meeting of the Karnataka State Decentralisation Planning and Development Committee here, he said a committee headed by the Rural Development and Panchayat Raj Minister would be formed to examine the recommendations of the Fifth State Finance Commission on fund allocation and administrative reforms. The committee would review the recommendations that could be implemented and submit a report, he said.
Under the Fifth State Finance Commission’s report, ₹1,261 crore has been released to gram panchayats, ₹557 crore to taluk panchayats and ₹183 crore to zilla panchayats, Mr. Shivakumar said.
The government would also take steps to improve the functioning of urban local bodies in keeping with the spirit of the 74th Constitutional Amendment. Experts from the National Law School of India University would be consulted on possible amendments to the relevant laws, he said.
Ward-level planning
The Chief Minister said urban local bodies should plan and implement development works through ward sabhas on the lines of gram sabhas. District, taluk and village-level planning committees have already been constituted, and they have been directed to meet once every three months and submit reports.
The Rural Development and Panchayat Raj and Urban Development departments have been asked to frame guidelines for implementing the ‘People’s Plan’, announced in the State Budget, to incorporate public needs from the grassroots into the State Budget. The departments should also develop the necessary software and provide funds to establish planning management units at the district and taluk levels, he said.
All departments have been asked to prepare responsibility maps defining their roles in implementing programmes related to gram, taluk and zilla panchayats and submit them within the stipulated time.
GST share for local bodies
Responding to the proposal to provide rural and urban local bodies a share in GST revenue, the Chief Minister said the government would submit a proposal to the GST Council. A proposal to establish the Karnataka Panchayat Administrative Service would also be sought from the Minister concerned.
He directed officials to expedite the demarcation of gram thana boundaries using data from the Centre’s SVAMITVA scheme, with the Panchayat Raj and Revenue departments working in coordination.
The government has also taken note of the loss of revenue to gram panchayats after the Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Board (KIADB) took over their power to levy taxes on industries. The law provides for 30% of the property tax collected by the authority to be shared with gram panchayats.
The Chief Minister asked officials to submit details of the total tax collected by the authority so far and the amount distributed to gram panchayats.

briefs.headline: Private unaided schools move Karnataka HC on delay in reimbursement of expenditure for RTE quota students
briefs.deck: Association of schools also seeks a national protocol for determination of ‘Per Child Expenditure’
briefs.bodyText:
The High Court of Karnataka has ordered issue of notice to the State government on a petition seeking fixation of ‘Per Child Expenditure’ (PCE) and reimbursement for the academic year 2026-27 to the unaided private schools towards 25% of the students admitted under the provisions of the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009.
Also, the court ordered issue of notice to the Central government on the plea for a national protocol for determining the PCE under Section 12(2) of the RTE Act.
Justice H.T. Narendra Prasad passed the order on a petition filed by the Associated Managements of Primary and Secondary Schools in Karnataka, which represents over 4,000 private unaided schools in the State.
It has been stated in the petition that Section 12(2) of the Act and Rule 8 of the Karnataka RTE Rules, 2012, mandate that the government notify the PCE annually before commencement of the academic year.
Pointing out that the PCE is the basis for reimbursing unaided schools that admit 25% of their students from disadvantaged groups and weaker sections under the RTE quota, the petitioner has complained that the failure to issue a fresh notification fixing the PCE and non-reimbursement of expenditure has forced schools to bear the cost of the RTE quota students leading to financial strain and potential fee hikes for the remaining 75% of students.
The association claimed that the last PCE revision was in 2017-18, with rates of ₹16,000 for primary and ₹8,000 for higher primary classes. Subsequent notifications since 2019 merely repeated these figures without any increase, despite rising expenditure on salaries, infrastructure, and welfare schemes, it has been contended in the petition.
While Rule 8 of the Karnataka RTE Rules prescribes a broad formula - total annual recurring expenditure divided by total enrolment - the petition points out that the law does not prescribe minimum accounting safeguards and lacks scientific methodology and structure to determine the PCE.
The national protocol should include parameters like a common definition of eligible recurring heads, uniform rules for allocation of composite expenditure, provisional pre-academic-year notification, audited year-end reconciliation, publication of worksheets, independent certification, and interest for delayed differential reimbursement, it has been sought in the petition.

briefs.headline: Cybersecurity workshop for micro, small and medium enterprises held in Bengaluru
briefs.deck: Government representatives, industry leaders, entrepreneurs and cybersecurity experts joined the event to discuss emerging cyber threats, regulatory compliance and measures to strengthen cybersecurity preparedness among MSMEs.
briefs.bodyText:
The Centre of Excellence for Cybersecurity–Karnataka (CySecK), an initiative of the State government, organised a one-day cybersecurity workshop for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) at the Indian Institute of Science (IISc) Bengaluru on Wednesday (October 14) to mark the Cybersecurity Awareness Month.
Government representatives, industry leaders, entrepreneurs and cybersecurity experts joined the event to discuss emerging cyber threats, regulatory compliance and measures to strengthen cybersecurity preparedness among MSMEs.
In a statement, CySecK said that the technical sessions focused on the evolving cybersecurity and regulatory landscape, cyber risks and compliance, risk management in cloud and artificial intelligence (AI) environments, defence strategies and cost-effective cybersecurity measures for MSMEs.
Experts also addressed cybersecurity challenges and practical approaches that smaller businesses could adopt to protect their digital assets and operations.

briefs.headline: Nine more taluks declared drought-hit in Karnataka; total rises to 226
briefs.deck: State to finalise memorandum seeking Centre’s assistance within a week; delegation likely to visit Delhi
briefs.bodyText:
Karnataka has declared nine more taluks drought-affected, taking the total to 226, Deputy Chief Minister and Revenue Minister G. Parameshwara said on Wednesday (October 14, 2026). The State government is preparing a final memorandum detailing the losses and seeking drought relief from the Centre, which is expected to be ready within a week.
The nine newly added taluks are Sakleshpur in Hassan district, which has been classified as severely drought-affected, and Khanapur in Belagavi; Hosanagara and Sagara in Shivamogga; Puttur, Moodbidri and Mulki in Dakshina Kannada; and Joida and Dandeli in Uttara Kannada, which have been classified as moderately drought-affected.
Speaking to reporters here, Mr. Parameshwara stated that field verification had been completed in the nine taluks. Assessment under the Trigger-1 criteria is still under way in some of the remaining taluks, and those meeting the prescribed conditions will be taken up for ground verification, he said.
The final estimate of drought-related losses and the amount of relief to be sought would be determined after the memorandum was completed, in accordance with National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF) guidelines, he said.
“Last year, we sought around ₹18,000 crore in drought relief. This year, losses have occurred across almost the entire State, and 226 taluks have already been declared drought-affected. If more taluks qualify, the losses will increase further,” he said.
Relax NDRF guidelines
The State government has asked the Centre to relax the NDRF guidelines for drought relief. Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar and Mr. Parameshwara have written to the Union government seeking a relaxation of the norms.
The Union Agriculture Minister had informed the State that the request would be examined, but no response has been received so far, Mr. Parameshwara said.
Once the memorandum is ready, the government will decide on sending a delegation led by the Chief Minister and the Deputy Chief Minister to Delhi to submit it to the Centre and seek assistance.
The government’s priority is to protect farmers’ livelihoods, provide relief for crop losses and safeguard rural communities affected by the drought, he said.
SC/ST reservation verdict
Mr. Parameshwara also said the State Cabinet would discuss the Karnataka High Court verdict on enhanced reservation for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes at its meeting on Thursday (October 15, 2026).
The Cabinet would decide whether the government should challenge the verdict in the Supreme Court or seek inclusion of the State’s reservation law in the Ninth Schedule of the Constitution, he said.
The High Court on October 12 struck down provisions of a 2022 State law that increased reservation for Scheduled Castes from 15% to 17% and for Scheduled Tribes from 3% to 7%, holding that the enhanced quota breached the 50% ceiling.
Mr. Parameshwara said further action would be taken after the Cabinet considered the judgment and decided on the government’s course of action.

briefs.headline: Karnataka generates record 2.04 crore person-days of rural employment since July
briefs.deck: Raichur tops districts with 24 lakh person-days; 87,164 new job cards issued this year
briefs.bodyText:
Karnataka has generated a record 2.04 crore person-days of employment under the VB-G RAM G scheme from July 1 to October 13, Rural Development and Panchayat Raj Minister Eshwar B. Khandre said on Wednesday.
During the corresponding period last year, 1.71 crore person-days were generated under the then Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS), he said.
The increase comes amid a rainfall deficit attributed to the El Niño effect, prompting the State to provide employment to more rural poor, Dalits, disadvantaged unskilled workers and landless labourers, Mr. Khandre said.
Raichur leads
Raichur, in the Kalyana Karnataka region, topped the State with 24 lakh person-days generated since July 1. Bidar followed with 21 lakh person-days, while Koppal ranked third with 18 lakh.
Compared with the corresponding period last year, employment generation rose by 340% in Vijayanagara, 257% in Kalaburagi, 207% in Koppal, 175% in Ballari and 173% in Bidar, according to the Minister.
The State has also issued 87,164 new job cards this year after undertaking e-KYC of existing MGNREGS job cards and organising job card melas. The initiative has helped families that would otherwise migrate in search of work find employment in their own areas, he said.
Focus on rural assets
Works taken up under the scheme include desilting of tanks, social forestry, restoration of canals, tanks and lakes, construction of cattle sheds and farm ponds, measures to prevent soil erosion on hill slopes, compost pits and rural connectivity roads.
The scheme has now been expanded to cover the construction of houses under housing schemes, community halls and rural bus stands. The aim is to create durable assets and support village development, Mr. Khandre said.
Under the VB-G RAM G scheme, each rural household can receive up to 125 days of employment a year. The wage is ₹382 a day, without any gender-based differentiation, enabling a household to earn up to ₹47,750 annually if it receives the full 125 days of work, he said.

stories.headline: Watsa's Prem-ium play in finance sector
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Hyderabad-born Prem Watsa, chairman of Fairfax Financial Holdings, with assets of around $100 billion, has always been upbeat on India and its growth prospects.
The Hyderabad Public School alumnus went to IIT Madras before pursuing an MBA in Canada, despite clearing the IIM entrance test.
Watsa, now 75, was once apprehended by the police while rushing to make it to a job interview at Confederation Life as there was a bank robbery nearby. But he managed to get a job before moving to Gardiner Watson 11 years later. In 1984, Watsa and Tony Hamblin, his former boss at Confederation Life, set up Hamblin Watsa Investment Counsel. Fairfax was formed in 1985 after Watsa refinanced a Canadian insurance company and changed the name to Fairfax Financial, derived from the principles of fair and friendly acquisitions.
He will have to put the principle to full use as he navigates the transition at 
IDBI Bank
, once a development financial institution.
Watsa is a big backer of financial services in India with Fairfax India, set up in 2014, portfolio reflecting that. Of the 13 investments, five were in the BFSI space, comprising 29% of the portfolio.
The 75-year-old investor's latest bet - a 60.7% stake in IDBI Bank for $5.6 billion- will further tilt the balance of the India portfolio towards financial services. 
Fairfax India's last balance sheet spoke of the immense opportunity in the sector given low levels of financial inclusion.
But it also means that Watsa - often referred to as Canada's Warren Buffet - and his team will have to rejig the portfolio in line with RBI regulations, including deciding the plan for Catholic Syrian Bank and Go Digit. IIFL Finance, IIFL Capital and 5paisa are also part of the portfolio. Beyond finance, currently, Bangalore International Airport is Fairfax's biggest bet in India.
Watsa is known for value-investing and looking for long-term returns. Fairfax India remains bullish on the economy. "In our view, India remains a land of immense opportunity!" its annual report said.

stories.headline: Government tops divestment target of 80k crore
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: With over five months to go for the fiscal year to close, Centre has topped its disinvestment and asset monetisation target of Rs 80,000 crore for 2026-27, with its kitty swelling to Rs 88,665 crore once the IDBI Bank stake sale is completed - providing much-needed cushion in a year, when it is burdened with higher fuel and fertiliser subsidies.
The Rs 26,500 crore from the IDBI transaction will add to the Rs 55,757 crore it has already raised from share sales, including the mega offer for sale of LIC shares that raked in over Rs 31,000 crore. Besides, it has mopped up Rs 6,367 crore through asset monetisation.
While more share sales on exchanges are under process, Rs 15,000-20,000 crore is targeted to be generated from InvITs, involving highways. There has also been talk of monetising some of the stadiums in the capital but it is still on the drawing board. There is uncertainty around the much-delayed transaction involving Hotel Ashok due to security concerns.
Even dividend flow is strong, with RBI announcing record dividend of nearly Rs 2.9 lakh crore and banks expected to deliver a bumper payout amid strong growth. RBI, banks and financial institutions were budgeted to pay just under Rs 3.2 lakh crore as dividends this year. Separately, PSUs have deposited Rs 17,773 crore in the treasury.
Officials said the revenue situation is also looking comfortabl,e with direct taxes showing steady rise, while GST is so far above target. Despite the hit due to reduction in levies on petrol, the Centre appears on course to better the indirect tax target.

stories.headline: Govt proposes BS-VII emission norms from April 2029; adds brake, tyre, battery-durability rules
stories.deck: India currently follows Bharat Stage VI standards, introduced nationwide in April 2020, which significantly tightened vehicle-emission requirements and brought the country closer to international regulatory practices
stories.bodyText:
The government has proposed introducing Bharat Stage VII (BS-VII) emission standards for passenger vehicles from April 1, 2029, tightening pollution controls through new limits on exhaust emissions, real-world driving tests and battery durability requirements.
According to a draft notification issued by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, the new rules would apply to category M1 vehicles — primarily passenger cars — manufactured from April 2029.
It invited public comments for 30 days before considering the draft amendments to the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989.
India currently follows Bharat Stage VI standards, introduced nationwide in April 2020, which significantly tightened vehicle-emission requirements and brought the country closer to international regulatory practices.
BS-VII standards would be introduced in phases, with additional requirements taking effect in April 2031 and April 2035, including controls on brake-particle emissions, tyre abrasion and particulate emissions across different powertrain technologies.
The proposal would require manufacturers to demonstrate compliance not only under laboratory conditions but also through real-world driving emissions tests and checks on vehicles already in service.
The draft sets a three-phase timeline of April 2029, April 2031 and April 2035, giving carmakers about two and a half years before the first limits bite. Component and tyre suppliers face separate deadlines, and several limits, such as tyre abrasion and some battery thresholds, are still to be notified. The rules cover electric vehicles for the first time through battery-durability and brake-particle requirements, and they push compliance monitoring into the vehicle itself.
Under the draft, the first phase from April 2029 would introduce BS-VII exhaust-emission limits for passenger vehicles, alongside requirements covering evaporative emissions, fuel consumption, electric energy consumption and battery durability.
Real-world driving tests would measure gaseous pollutants and particle numbers, while on-board systems would monitor emissions and fuel or energy consumption. The draft also envisages an Environmental Vehicle Passport giving users access to information on vehicle emissions, fuel consumption and battery health.
From April 2031, the proposed framework would introduce brake-particle emission limits and tyre-abrasion requirements. The draft sets a brake-particle mass limit of 3 milligrams per kilometre for pure electric vehicles and 7 mg per km for other specified powertrain categories.
Further requirements are scheduled for April 2035, including a common brake-particle mass limit across powertrain technologies and additional particle-number controls, subject to limits to be notified separately.
The proposed standards cover a range of powertrains and fuels, including petrol, diesel, compressed natural gas, ethanol blends, hydrogen and hybrid vehicles, as well as electric vehicles for applicable energy-consumption and battery requirements.
For M1 vehicles, the draft sets carbon monoxide limit at 1,000 mg per km for positive-ignition (petrol-type) engines and 500 mg per km for compression-ignition (diesel) engines. Nitrogen oxides (NOx) limits have been set at 60 mg per km for positive-ignition and 80 mg per km for compression-ignition.
Particulate limits have been proposed at 4.5 mg per km for both engine types.
The limits apply across fuels, including petrol blended with 20% ethanol (E20), diesel, CNG, LPG, hydrogen, methanol, and flex-fuel and bi-fuel vehicles.
The draft also regulates non-exhaust emissions and vehicle durability. From April 1, 2031, limits on brake particle emissions (PM10) are set by powertrain. They are 3 mg per km for pure electric vehicles and 7 mg per km for hybrids, fuel-cell vehicles and internal combustion vehicles. From April 1, 2035, a single 3 mg per km limit applies to all powertrains.
Abrasion limits for C1 tyres are to apply from April 1, 2031, with the limits to be notified separately.
For pure electric vehicles and plug-in hybrids, batteries must retain at least 75% performance for the first five years or 100,000 km, and 67% up to eight years or 160,000 km, whichever comes first.
From April 1, 2030, type approval will include on-road emission tests using portable measurement systems, with a conformity factor of 1.0 for NOx and particle number, according to the draft.
Vehicles must carry on-board diagnostics, on-board monitoring able to detect emissions at least 2.5 times the limit, and on-board fuel and electric energy consumption monitoring. Fuel-consumption data must be accessible from April 1, 2030, and the monitoring data from April 1, 2032, including over-the-air.
Emission compliance must be maintained for 160,000 km or eight years, with an additional lifetime period to 200,000 km or 10 years.
Buyers would get an Environmental Vehicle Passport showing fuel consumption, battery state of health and pollutant emissions, with provision for in-vehicle display, the draft rules said.
The draft also allows petrol-type and diesel vehicles fitted with geofencing technology to be approved as 'BS-VII-G' vehicles. Manufacturers must declare and label ethanol compatibility above E20.

stories.headline: Centre sets up panel to study problems of sugarcane farmers
stories.deck: Representatives of sugarcane farmers from Karnataka and Maharashtra had met Union Ministers demanding that the government must increase remunerative returns to sugarcane farmers
stories.bodyText:
The Union Government, on Tuesday (October 13, 2026), constituted a four-member panel headed by former member of NITI Aayog Ramesh Chand to examine issues raised by sugarcane farmers and recommend “appropriate measures” for addressing their concerns. Representatives of sugarcane farmers from Karnataka and Maharashtra had met Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan and Union Minister of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution Pralhad Joshi demanding that the government must increase remunerative returns to sugarcane farmers.
A release issued by the Union Food Ministry said the panel will examine the demand taking into account cultivation costs and other relevant factors. “It will also examine the demand for revision of the ex-mill Minimum Selling Price (MSP) of sugar in the context of sugar production costs, market realisations, and the financial viability of sugar mills,” it said.
“Other key areas of examination will include existing mechanisms for testing and reporting sugar recovery, measures to ensure transparent verification of recovery, and prevailing sugarcane weighment practices at sugar mills, including the adequacy of calibration, inspection and verification mechanisms,” the release added.
The Committee will also examine prevailing practices, relating to deductions from the weight of mechanically harvested sugarcane and assess the extent of actual losses, if any, arising from mechanised harvesting. “It will evaluate the financial impact of the present practices on the cane price payable to farmers and may consider any other related matters deemed necessary,” the government said.
The Committee will consult all stakeholders, including farmers’ representatives, sugar mill associations, State Governments and other experts or organisations, as considered necessary. “The Committee will submit its report, containing its findings and specific recommendations, as early as possible, for consideration by the competent authority,” the statement added.
Apart from Prof. Chand, the panel comprises the Agriculture Commissioner, Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare; Joint Secretary (Sugar), Department of Food and Public Distribution and Joint Secretary (Legal Metrology), Department of Consumer Affairs as members.
