briefs.headline: Rupee rises for 4th day, up 19 paise vs dollar
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: The rupee appreciated 19 paise to close at 95.17 against the US dollar on Wednesday, registering the fourth straight session of gains, supported by RBI interventions designed to ease near-term dollar demand and limit speculative foreign exchange exposure.
Forex traders said the Indian rupee rose to a one-month high on RBI's measures to curb speculative bets. A weak dollar and easing of US Treasury yields also aided the rupee. However, weak domestic markets capped sharp gains. At the interbank foreign exchange market, the rupee opened at 95.05 against the dollar and touched the intraday low of 94.76 against the greenback.
On Tuesday, the rupee strengthened for the third straight session and appreciated 42 paise to close at 95.36. In the last four trading sessions, the rupee has gained 171 paise . "We expect the rupee to trade with a positive bias on RBI's intervention to curb excessive speculation in the rupee. A weak dollar and a decline in US Treasury yields may also support the rupee," an analyst said. Agencies

briefs.headline: IDBI sale to increase value, new management to get free hand
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: The sale of govt stake in 
IDBI Bank
 will help increase its value, fully protect the interest of employees and directors nominated by the Centre and LIC will exit the board to give the new management a free hand, a top govt official told TOI on Wednesday.
Hours after govt nod, Dipam secretary Arunish Chawla also vowed to move ahead with other transactions in the coming months and "not rest on past laurels". "We still haven't finished our work. We are further energised by the approval... We will continue to move ahead with the strategic transactions, and we will take Cabinet approvals to their logical conclusions. You will keep hearing from us from time to time," he said, without commenting on specific companies.
Since 2016, the Union Cabinet has cleared three dozen strategic disinvestments but several of them, including BPCL and Shipping Corporation are no longer being pursued. Chawla dismissed suggestions that govt was not keen on privatisation of PSUs. "We are delivering on what has been approved by the Cabinet and we have completed five strategic sales in the last five years... Govt remains firmly on the track of reforms.
"
The secretary said the new owners will bring fresh energy and private sector management practices and efficiency to boost IDBI Bank's performance, while expecting the transaction to be closed before end of the current financial year.
"We have spent the last one year discussing with the management, the employee associations, the qualified parties. We've brought everyone on board. Even today the service conditions of the IDBI Bank employees is decided by its board. The service conditions of all existing employees will be fully protected, all pensioners of IDBI Bank will be fully protected. There is a special pension fund set aside for this purpose and going forward, the new management will run the bank in consultation with the employees and its associations."
Chawla said a lot of hard work has gone into ensuring that the transaction was cleared. After the setback in March, when the bids were rejected, the core group on disinvestment led by the Cabinet secretary and DIPAM went back to the drawing board. "We relied completely on professional advice. When the stock market price is extremely volatile and the stock is very narrowly traded, it tends to misalign the intrinsic value," he said.
So, govt studied global examples and went for relative valuation by what is called market multiple method or moon charts methodology. The market multiples of comparable entities are used to compute the fair market value. Separately, an asset valuation method was used based on the assets and liabilities.
"Because the book value of IDBI Bank was low, the professional agencies converted the asset and liabilities on the books, including financial assets and physical assets like land and buildings, into their fair replacement value. In addition, they valued intangibles like the economic value of the banking licence, customer relationship, which is built on its branch network, the brand value and added all this up to the book value to arrive at the net asset value or the fair value asset value," Chawla added.
Using the average of the two valuations worked out to Rs 75.99 a share, while the winning best bid was Rs 81 a share, resulting in CCEA clearing the Farifax offer.
"After six months of hard work and through a collective decision and multi-lauyered decision making process, where everyone's views were taken on board and professional agencies were allowed to do their job, we have been able to find a way forward... We have stood up to take difficult decisions and that is what is necessary to drive reforms."

briefs.headline: Wholesale inflation touches 30-month high
briefs.bodyText:
New Delhi: Factory gate inflation based on the wholesale price index (WPI) surged to a 30 month high of 11.4% in Sept from 9.9% in Aug, as rising fuel and manufactured goods prices pushed inflation into double digits, the official data released Wednesday showed. In comparison, WPI stood at -0.2% in Sept 2025.
Data shows fuel and power inflation accelerated to 25.9% in Sept from 22.9% in Aug as prices for crude petroleum, natural gas and mineral oil continued to rise, amid uncertainty surrounding key maritime chokepoints due to renewed hostilities in West Asia.
Inflation in manufactured products, which account for nearly two-thirds of the WPI basket, rose to 9.8% from 8.4% in Aug, with acceleration being particularly sharp in basic metals (17%), chemicals and chemical products (16.7%), textiles and rubber products (13.7%) and electrical equipment (12%).
CareEdge chief economist Rajani Sinha said India's crude basket and spot brent crude prices are trading well above brent futures, indicating tightness in the physical supply of crude. "While retail fuel prices have remained unchanged, oil marketing companies have raised bulk diesel prices, which are now nearly Rs 50-60 per litre higher than retail prices. Persistently elevated crude prices could increase freight, agricultural and irrigation and transportation costs, which could indirectly feed into the retail inflation," she added.
 Food prices also contributed to the Sept increase as WPI Food Index rose to 8.7% from 7.1% in Aug, continuing an upward trend seen over recent month.
Though RBI tracks consumer price index (CPI) based retail inflation for its policy rate setting, the former tends to feed into the latter, albeit with a lag. Official data released Monday showed retail inflation inching to 5.5% in Sept from 4.8% in Aug.

briefs.headline: Currency depreciation key headwind for foreign investors: Blackstone's Gray
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: Its $50 billion investments in India place Blackstone among the top 10 business houses. The world's largest alternative asset manager plans to double its investments in the next five years mainly in private equity and real estate, and expand into infrastructure, credit and growth investing. In an interview with TOI, Jonathan Gray, president and COO of Blackstone, speaks of how the focus is on building businesses.
Despite being the fastest-growing large economy, India is witnessing capital outflows. What ails foreign investment?
The energy-price shock from the war, rising interest rates, AI disruption fears in IT services and India's once-high market valuations have triggered a correction. Yet, underlying growth remains strong, with the PM citing nearly 8% economic growth and market earnings expected to rise at mid-teens rates in Q3.
For long-term investors, the reset offers a better entry point, with lower valuations improving opportunities for new capital. Markets may turn fickle, but sustained earnings growth should draw global capital back. We see this as a temporary cold patch and will continue investing.
Does currency depreciation worry you? What needs to be done?
Currency depreciation has been the biggest headwind for foreign investors, making faster-growing businesses a better bet than bond-like assets with flat returns. 
We focus on high-growth healthcare, financial services, travel, digital infrastructure and real estate, including malls, offices and warehouses. India has made major strides in physical infrastructure, from airports and flyovers to GST reform, digital payments, legal systems and capital markets. These improvements have opened sectors once inaccessible to investors like us. So, rather than focus only on what govt can do better, it is important to stop and say they have done a heck of a job.
Last year, you spoke about making delisting easier...
India's 90% shareholding threshold for delisting is among the world's highest. Some of the rules are there to protect minority shareholders from promoters, but I think there's a way to do that and allow some of these companies to be privatised (delisted). Reforms can unlock consolidation, reward shareholders and improve companies' access to capital, as Japan's liberalisation has shown. It is like refreshing the farm by turning the soil.
Yet, there have been some major capital-market strides. The REIT market, once non-existent, has attracted billions in capital, enabled us to bring five out of six REITs to the market and a $1.3 billion secondary sale in Knowledge Realty Trust in Aug. India is the world's second-most liquid IPO market after the US. Greater regulatory and tax certainty remains a work in progress, but govt deserves credit for opening markets to foreign capital. Further reforms could deepen access to capital.
In AI, which areas would you look at investing in?
AI opportunities span data centres, neoclouds and IT services. As traditional IT work shifts to AI, firms such as Mphasis, in which we own a large stake, are becoming AI-deployment partners, helping businesses redesign workflows rather than simply adopt tools such as Claude. Energy, especially renewables, will also be critical to powering both India's growth and its expanding data-centre infra.
What risks do you see in AI investments?
There is a risk of overinvestment and capital misallocation in AI, but financial commentary is too negative. Usage is surging, with tangible productivity gains. At IGI, our diamond and jewellery certification business in India, AI visualisation tools make grading 40% faster and enable each employee to process 30% more diamonds.
Demand is exploding, driven by businesses and individuals using personalised AI agents, while computing capacity remains constrained by shortages of land, power, chips and capital. Unlike the '90s telecom boom, when speculative, leveraged infrastructure outstripped demand, today's data-centre build-out has strong demand, investment-grade hyperscalers as offtakers and little speculative construction. It is therefore financially sounder than booms seen in the past.
But telecom companies did take a hit when Starlink announced its foray into telecom...
AI's biggest risk is disruption to legacy businesses, already reflected in falling software and professional-services valuations and questions over the future of billable hours. Some AI investments will fail, but the technology's productivity gains and growth potential make significant infrastructure investment compelling.
Investment in computing infrastructure can be compared to aviation, where aircraft retain value despite airline failures. Likewise, scarce AI computing capacity can be redeployed if an LLM company, software firm or hyperscaler fails. Markets may underestimate this residual value. Most data centres are backed by 15-20-year contracts with trillion-dollar-plus companies, limiting speculative, leveraged construction.
You earlier spoke about risks arising from conflicts and macro factors. At the same time, many countries, including India, are seeing unrest. Do you see this impacting business?
In a world connected by social media, we have seen a rise in social unrest, and I think that's going to be more of a staple of societies going forward because organising is now much easier. Part of it is also that we have seen a sharp rise in the cost of living, energy costs, food costs and housing costs, and I think this is something govts are going to need to respond to. I think in the West, we've made it very difficult to build new energy, new infrastructure and new housing, and I hope there's a push for some regulatory and permitting reform to accelerate investment in those areas. Technological upheaval also breeds anxiety, as during past industrial revolutions, while wars add to cost pressures. Hopefully, these wars will end at some point, and that should reduce pressure on prices. Economic growth is critical to getting countries through this, and countries will have to control the cost of living through fiscal discipline and low inflation.

briefs.headline: US stocks fall as inflation accelerates; S&P 500 drops 1.1%, Nasdaq slides 1.6%
briefs.deck: Wall Street faced a noticeable dip in stock prices following a surprise rise in inflation data, which has raised concerns over borrowing costs. As Treasury yields soared, investors pondered the shifting allure between equities and bonds. Major banks explored both the potential gains and risks tied to investments in the artificial intelligence sector. Although AI infrastructure is evolving, rising…
briefs.bodyText:
Wall Street stocks fell on Wednesday as hotter-than-expected US inflation data pushed Treasury yields higher, adding to concerns about borrowing costs even as major banks assessed the opportunities and risks associated with the artificial intelligence (AI) investment boom.
The S&P 500 fell 1.1%, putting it on track for its fifth decline in six sessions since hitting a record high. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 171 points, or 0.3%, while the Nasdaq Composite declined 1.6%, as of 1:14 pm Eastern time.
US consumer prices rose 3.7% year on year in September, accelerating from 3.4% in August and exceeding economists’ expectations of 3.6%. The data fuelled concerns that inflation could remain elevated, partly due to rising energy prices amid the war with Iran.
The benchmark 10-year US Treasury yield climbed to 5.23%, after briefly crossing 5.32% during the session. Higher yields can weigh on equities by increasing borrowing costs and making bonds more attractive relative to stocks.
Meanwhile, executives at major US banks highlighted the opportunities presented by AI infrastructure investment, while cautioning that uncertainty over demand, financing costs and returns could create risks.
Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon said the long-term demand for capital and computing capacity required by the AI ecosystem remained uncertain.
“No one knows how the demands for capital and compute will evolve as the broader AI ecosystem matures,” Solomon said, stressing the need for vigilance in financing decisions and risk management.
Citigroup CEO Jane Fraser, however, said investment in the broader AI ecosystem was not slowing, citing an ongoing shortage of computing capacity.
The AI infrastructure expansion, driven by heavy investment in data centres and computing power, presents banks with opportunities to finance large-scale projects. However, elevated interest rates could raise project costs, squeeze returns and make debt repayment more difficult.
Wells Fargo CEO Charlie Scharf described the AI buildout as a significant economic force, bringing both opportunities and risks because of the substantial borrowing involved and pressure on prices across some industries and supply chains.
Banks are also deploying AI internally to improve productivity and reduce costs, although the financial benefits vary. Fraser said Citi was developing products up to 40% faster using AI and had reduced technology vendor expenses by 30% through coding tools.
Investors are watching whether such efficiency gains can justify the heavy spending on AI. Concerns are also mounting over cybersecurity threats and the risks posed by AI agents capable of taking actions autonomously.
The combination of persistent inflation, elevated bond yields and uncertainty over AI investment returns has added to the challenges facing Wall Street, where high stock valuations leave limited room for corporate earnings or productivity gains to disappoint.

briefs.headline: ‘Not benefiting anyone’: Traders urge Rahul to rethink SIR protests amid festive season, cite business losses
briefs.deck: Traders' groups are appealing to Rahul Gandhi to rethink the current protests affecting business as the festive season approaches. They express concerns over road blockades, which are deterring shoppers and complicating delivery schedules, particularly for small vendors. With Diwali around the corner, many are struggling to stockpile supplies due to these disruptions. Trade representatives are…
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Traders’ associations have urged Congress leader Rahul Gandhi to reconsider the ongoing protests against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and issues concerning Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, alleging that demonstrations and road blockades in the national capital are hurting businesses ahead of Diwali.
Representatives of trade bodies said traders stock up on goods and often take loans ahead of the festive season, relying on increased sales to meet annual expenses. They claimed that disruptions were keeping customers away, restricting market access and affecting deliveries, with small traders bearing the brunt.
Ajay Gupta, a member of the National Traders Welfare Board, said “I humbly request the Leader of the Opposition, Shri Rahul Gandhi ji, to reconsider the agitation currently underway, as it is not benefiting anyone; instead, it is creating an atmosphere of anarchy,” he said. “We are not opposed to the act of protesting itself ... but it should be done in a manner that causes no harm to the common man and creates no obstacles for us traders in running our businesses,” he added.
Meanwhile, Ghanshyam Das Goyal of the Dal and Besan Millers Association said traders from areas around Delhi usually visit the capital to purchase stocks for Diwali, but the disruptions had discouraged them from coming. 
Prakash Purgal of the Bangalore Wholesale Cloth Merchant Association also urged Rahul to pursue dialogue instead of road blockades, warning that closures during the Dussehra-Diwali and wedding season could hurt small businesses. “The Navratri festival is currently underway. Traders from areas surrounding Delhi usually come to the city to purchase stock for the Diwali season; however, due to the commotion you have stirred up, people have stopped visiting Delhi,”
Prakash Purgal, representing the Bangalore Wholesale Cloth Merchant Association, also urged Rahul to ensure that protests did not lead to road blockades during the festive season. He said Dussehra, Diwali and the wedding season were crucial for traders, who had begun to see a recovery after a prolonged period of business difficulties.
Warning that road blockades could force small traders to shut their shops, Purgal called for disputes to be resolved through dialogue.
“Please consider this carefully: whatever issues need to be discussed should be addressed through dialogue, rather than by blocking roads and spoiling the festive spirit of Dussehra and Diwali,” he said.
Several trade bodies from Delhi, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Karnataka and Kerala submitted representations on October 12 and 13, seeking steps to ensure that protests do not obstruct commercial activity during the festive season.
The traders’ appeal comes amid an intensifying INDIA bloc campaign against the Election Commission’s functioning under Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The Opposition has demanded Kumar’s resignation, scrapping of the SIR exercise and restoration of deleted voter names, alleging irregularities in the revision process. It has also called for a return to ballot papers instead of electronic voting machines (EVMs), restoration of pre-SIR electoral rolls for future elections and an effective appeals mechanism for voters excluded from the rolls. The bloc has pursued protests and legal action as part of its wider “Save Democracy” campaign.

briefs.headline: Hyundai to invest additional ₹4,000 crore in Pune plant, to raise output to 3,20,000 units
briefs.bodyText:
Hyundai Motor India Ltd. on Wednesday announced to invest an additional ₹4,000 crore in it’s Pune plant by 2030 taking the total investment to ₹11,000 crore.
The plant’s current annual installed capacity of 1,70,000 units, is set to scale up in phases to 3,20,000 units by 2030, it’s MD & CEO Tarun Garg said.
The company has announced to increase it’s localisation from 83% to 92%.
The plant, the company’s second after Chennai, was on Wednesday formally inaugurated by Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis.
Euisun Chung, Executive Chair - Hyundai Motor Group (HMG); Jaehoon Chang, Vice Chair - HMG; José Muñoz, President & CEO - Hyundai Motor Company (HMC) were present on the occasion.
HMIL also celebrated the achievement of cumulative exports of 4 million passenger vehicles from India since 1999, underscoring the company’s contribution towards establishing India as a global automotive manufacturing and export hub.
Euisun Chung, Executive Chair - HMG, said, “India remains one of Hyundai’s most important and strategic markets globally. The inauguration of the Pune plant reflects our long-term commitment to India’s growth and our confidence in its bright future.”
“HMIL’s milestone of 4 million cumulative vehicle exports demonstrates the global competitiveness of Indian manufacturing and highlights India’s growing role within Hyundai Motor Group’s worldwide operations,” he added.
Beyond manufacturing, HMIL is committed to contributing to India’s future through innovation, research, electrification and talent development.
The company is working with Indian institutions and partners through Industry-academia partnerships, battery and electrification research initiatives and future mobility programs to help shape the next chapter of sustainable mobility.
The Pune plant located at Talegaon is Hyundai’s global production hub of Venue. It also houses a engine shop with advanced manufacturing technologies, producing 150,000 engines annually to support vehicle production.

briefs.headline: India remains top Russian crude buyer in September despite 29% fall in imports since July
briefs.deck: India has remained the largest destination for Russian crude oil, although imports decreased significantly from peak levels. In September, India imported around 1.82 million barrels per day, while competition from China intensified. US sanctions and tariffs have influenced purchasing decisions but supply constraints also played a crucial role. Venezuelan crude has returned to India's oil imports…
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: India remained the world's largest destination for Russian crude oil in September, although imports fell nearly 29 per cent from July levels as Chinese refiners stepped up purchases and tightened the availability of Russian supplies, according to ship-tracking data from Kpler.
India imported around 1.82 million barrels per day (bpd) of Russian crude in September, compared with China's 1.49 million bpd. Indian imports had peaked at 2.6 million bpd in June and 2.57 million bpd in July before declining to 2.02 million bpd in August.
The moderation comes amid US pressure on countries buying Russian oil, including through tariffs and sanctions. However, analysts say the decline in India's purchases also reflects supply constraints and growing competition from China, rather than being solely a response to Washington's actions.
"The recent moderation in India's Russian imports is not simply a response to US tariff pressure; tighter availability and stronger competition from China have also played an important role," said Sumit Ritolia, senior manager (modelling) at Kpler.
Chinese refiners have increased their purchases of Russian crude in recent months, partly because of reduced access to Iranian oil, adding to competition for available supplies.
Based on cargoes currently being tracked, Kpler expects India's Russian crude imports to remain broadly stable at around 1.8 million to 1.9 million bpd in October.
US pressure over Russian oil, but a diesel deal with Moscow
India's continued reliance on Russian crude comes amid Washington's efforts to discourage purchases of Russian energy. US President Donald Trump signed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 into law in September. The legislation authorises tariffs of up to 100 per cent on imports from countries buying Russian oil, but gives the president discretion over whether and how to apply them. India and China are among the major buyers potentially affected.
However, Washington's own approach to Russian energy has also shifted in response to rising fuel costs.
On October 9, Trump announced an agreement with Russian President Vladimir Putin under which Russia would supply more than 300,000 tonnes of diesel to US and global markets, followed by additional shipments. The Trump administration also temporarily eased US sanctions on Russian fuel to facilitate the arrangement, which was aimed at increasing supplies and containing prices ahead of the November midterm elections.
The move nevertheless drawn criticism from Ukraine and some European leaders, who argue that purchases of Russian energy could provide Moscow with additional revenue during its war against Ukraine.
Meanwhile, alongside Russian supplies, Venezuelan crude has regained a place in India's import mix this year after remaining largely absent in recent years. Shipments began accelerating from April, according to Kpler.
Venezuela exported around 250,000 bpd of crude to India in August and 257,000 bpd in September. The US remained the larger destination, receiving approximately 452,000 bpd in August and 563,000 bpd in September.

stories.headline: UCL Round-up: PSG sink Man City, Mourinho's Madrid stage late comeback
stories.deck: The Champions League set a new scoring record with 78 goals during Matchday 2. Paris Saint-Germain defeated Manchester City 4-2, while Real Madrid scored three late goals to beat Roma 4-3. Liverpool won 6-3 against LASK, and Real Betis edged Porto 3-2. Aston Villa also secured a commanding 6-0 victory over Fenerbahçe on a thrilling night.
stories.bodyText:
The 
UEFA Champions League
 witnessed a record-breaking night of goals on Wednesday, as Paris Saint-Germain defeated Manchester City 4-2 and Real Madrid scored three late goals to beat Roma 4-3.
A total of 78 goals were scored across Matchday 2, surpassing the previous record of 71 goals set during Matchday 3 last season. Six of Wednesday’s nine matches featured at least five goals, with Liverpool’s 6-3 victory over LASK among the highest-scoring games.
PSG stun Manchester City, Real Madrid stage comeback
PSG delivered a strong first-half performance in Manchester, scoring three times before the break. Désiré Doué opened the scoring in the 13th minute and then assisted Ousmane Dembélé shortly afterwards. Vitinha added the third in the 32nd minute, leaving City struggling to respond.
Erling Haaland pulled one back in the 53rd minute, but Maghnes Akliouche restored PSG’s three-goal advantage. Haaland scored again in the 75th minute, bringing City back into the contest, but PSG held on for the win. The match was Manchester City’s first European fixture since being charged with financial rule breaches in the Premier League.
Real Madrid produced a dramatic finish against Roma. After the home side took a 3-1 lead, Madrid substitutes Carlos Espí and Endrick scored late goals to level the match.
Antonio Rüdiger then netted the winner from close range following a corner, securing a 4-3 victory. Kylian Mbappé also scored on his 100th Champions League appearance, becoming the youngest player to reach that milestone at 27.
Liverpool, Betis and other results
Liverpool defeated LASK 6-3, with Bradley Barcola scoring a hat trick. Ronald Araújo, Jeremie Frimpong and Lewis Koumas also found the net for Liverpool, while LASK scored three times in response.
Real Betis beat Porto 3-2 in a heated contest, with Isco scoring the decisive penalty late in the game. Abde Ezzalzouli also scored a spectacular goal for Betis.
Elsewhere, Aston Villa thrashed Fenerbahçe 6-0, Bodø/Glimt beat Borussia Dortmund 1-0, and Stuttgart defeated Slovan Bratislava 3-0. Shakhtar Donetsk overcame AEK Athens 3-1 in London, while Feyenoord came from behind to defeat Como 3-2.

stories.headline: Farhan, now Pakistan's captain, surpasses Abhishek to script new T20I record
stories.deck: Pakistan captain Sahibzada Farhan set a new record with 238 runs in a three-match T20I series against Sri Lanka, surpassing Abhishek Sharma’s 229 runs. Despite Farhan’s third consecutive half-century, Pakistan lost the final match by eight wickets. Kusal Mendis starred with an unbeaten 87, helping Sri Lanka win the match, while Pakistan secured the series 2-1.
stories.bodyText:
Pakistan captain Sahibzada Farhan created a new record by scoring 238 runs in a three-match T20I series against Sri Lanka, surpassing India's Abhishek Sharma, who scored 229 runs against Afghanistan earlier this year.
Farhan scored his third consecutive half-century, making 76 off 47 balls in the final match on Tuesday.
Farhan breaks Abhishek Sharma’s record
Farhan now leads the list for the most runs in a bilateral three-match men's T20I series between two Full Member teams. New Zealand's Colin Munro is third with 223 runs, followed by Australia's David Warner with 217 and Afghanistan's Hazratullah Zazai with 204.
Despite Farhan's strong performance, Pakistan lost the third T20I by eight wickets. The hosts scored 168/8, but Sri Lanka chased down the target with 17 balls remaining, thanks to Kusal Mendis's unbeaten 87 off 47 balls. Mendis was named Player of the Match.
Pakistan had already won the series after victories in the first two matches, winning the opening game by four wickets and the second by 82 runs.
After the final match, Farhan said Pakistan had followed the same plan as in the earlier games and stressed the importance of staying in form.
"The way we set a superb target in the first two matches, today also we had the same plan, but it's cricket; anything can happen. The effort is to stay consistent. When I perform well, I'm even more focused to do well in the next match. It's cricket; you're not always in form. So I'm looking to make the most of it," he said, as per the ICC website.
Kusal Mendis praises Sri Lanka’s performance
Sri Lanka captain Kusal Mendis praised his team's bowling, fielding and batting after the convincing win. He also highlighted Kamindu Mendis's contribution following the Powerplay.
"We bowled really well today in the middle period. The fielding was better too, and the batting was excellent. Kamindu (Mendis) batted really well after the Powerplay. He played his natural game, and I did too. We did really well in all three departments," he said.

stories.headline: PSG downs Man City 4-2 in pulsating Champions League clash
stories.deck: Real Madrid edges Roma 4-3 in seven-goal thriller; Haaland becomes fastest player to 60 Champions League goals
stories.bodyText:
Twice-defending champions Paris Saint-Germain beat Manchester City 4-2 in a pulsating Champions League encounter on Wednesday, their devastating first-half display proving decisive against a City side playing under a cloud of scrutiny.
On a breathless night featuring 46 goals, Bradley Barcola scored a hat-trick in Liverpool's 6-3 thrashing of LASK, Aston Villa recorded the biggest European victory in their history with a 6-0 thrashing of Fenerbahce and Real Madrid staged a stunning late comeback to beat AS Roma 4-3.
But no fixture carried more intrigue than the Etihad clash, where City played their first home game since being found guilty of 114 breaches of financial rules.
City, who have denied all wrongdoing and appealed the verdict, were carved open by PSG in the first half.
PSG'S first-half blitz
Desire Doue and Ousmane Dembele scored less than two minutes apart before Warren Zaire-Emery's clever touch released Vitinha to drive the third beyond Gianluigi Donnarumma in the 32nd minute.
City emerged transformed after the break and Erling Haaland headed in Iliman Ndiaye's cross in the 53rd minute to become the fastest player to reach 60 Champions League goals, hitting the landmark in 60 games compared with Lionel Messi’s previous record of 80.
City's joy was short-lived as Maghnes Akliouche's stunning long-range strike found the net despite Donnarumma getting a hand to it.
Haaland had the City fans on their feet when he swept home Ayyoub Bouaddi's pass in the 75th minute for his second, before Donnarumma made up for his blunder by saving a penalty from Ferran Torres.
The match unfolded against an "us against the world" backdrop, with City fans in the South Stand holding up cards that read "CTID" (City Till I Die).
Former City manager Pep Guardiola watched from the stands alongside chairman Khaldoon Al-Mubarak and senior executives Ferran Soriano and Hugo Viana.
Villa hits Fenerbahce for six
At Villa Park, Nicolas Jackson and Ross Barkley both scored twice in a dominant display by the hosts. Johan Manzambi opened the scoring in the 12th minute before Jackson struck in the 31st and 39th minutes to give Villa a commanding halftime lead.
Barkley added a fourth from the penalty spot in the 68th minute before grabbing his second four minutes later, while Tammy Abraham completed the rout with a stoppage-time strike.
At the Stadio Olimpico, Real Madrid scored three times in the closing stages to overturn a two-goal deficit.
Marten de Roon gave Roma the lead in the 20th minute before Kylian Mbappe equalised five minutes later, but Donyell Malen struck twice in the 51st and 57th minutes to put the hosts in control.
However, the visitors mounted a remarkable comeback as Carlos Espi pulled a goal back in the 82nd minute before Endrick levelled three minutes later.
Former Roma defender Antonio Ruediger then completed the turnaround in the 90th minute, holding off his marker to steer home Arda Guler's inswinging corner from close range and snatch victory for the Spanish side.

Liverpool's Bradley Barcola scored his first goals for the club with a hat-trick as they swept aside Champions League newcomers LASK 6-3 on Wednesday, spoiling the Austrian side's first home game in Europe's elite club competition.

briefs.headline: 5 wickets in an over! SA bowler makes history with rare feat - Watch
briefs.deck: Laycock finished with career-best figures of 6/26, including a record of four wickets in four consecutive deliveries in South African T20 cricket.
briefs.bodyText:
Chad Laycock made history on Tuesday by becoming the first bowler to take five wickets in an over in South African T20 cricket. The 19-year-old achieved the feat while playing for KZN Inland against Titans in the CSA Pro20 Cup in Pietermaritzburg.
Laycock finished with career-best figures of 6/26, including a record of four wickets in four consecutive deliveries in South African T20 cricket. Among Full Member teams in T20 internationals, Lasith Malinga, Rashid Khan, Curtis Campher and Jason Holder have previously achieved the four-wicket sequence.
Laycock also set a new record for the best bowling figures in CSA Pro20 Cup history, going past Beuran Hendricks' 6/29 from 2014.
The historic over came in the 19th over of the Titans innings. Laycock first dismissed Leus du Plooy before taking the wickets of Dayyaan Galiem, Aphiwe Mnyanda, Janco Smit and Esosa Aihevba off the next four deliveries. The five wickets ended Titans' innings at 204, with the team having been 193/4 before the over.
Laycock had earlier given KZN Inland their first breakthrough by dismissing Lhuan-dre Pretorius, who scored 81 off 36 balls, in the ninth over. 
Pretorius and his opening partner had put together 112 runs.
However, Laycock's performance was not enough to secure a win for KZN Inland. Chasing 205, they finished on 183/6, losing the match by 21 runs. Laycock remained unbeaten on 31. The victory extended table-toppers Titans' unbeaten run in the competition to six matches.
Laycock became the fourth bowler known to have taken five wickets in an over in men's T20 cricket, as per Cricinfo. Bangladesh's Al-Amin Hossain, India's Abhimanyu Mithun and Indonesia's Gede Priandana had achieved the feat before him.
Priandana remains the only bowler, male or female, to take five wickets in an over in a T20 international. He achieved the feat against Cambodia in December 2025.
Al-Amin took five wickets in an over while playing for UCB-BCB XI against Abahani Limited in the 2013-14 Victory Day T20 Cup. Mithun achieved the feat in the 2019-20 Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy semifinal, playing for Karnataka against Haryana in India's domestic T20 competition.

briefs.headline: Sai Sudharsan gathering info before the tour down under
briefs.bodyText:
B. Sai Sudharsan said on Wednesday that the National selectors had asked him to play in the Ranji Trophy as part of his preparation for India’s upcoming tour of New Zealand.
Having been on India-A duty in Puducherry, he arrived here “at 10.40 p.m.” on the eve of Tamil Nadu’s Ranji Trophy opener against Rajasthan (October 10).
“There was a day’s break between games in Puducherry. On that day (October 10), our manager told me that the selectors had asked me to play the Ranji Trophy.
“After the first day’s play here, I spoke with Pragyan Ojha (interim chief National selector). He said it would be good for the upcoming New Zealand series — for preparation and all. That was the clarity from their side.”
He has been “watching a lot of old videos” of India’s Tests in New Zealand to understand the conditions and how best to bat there.
“I have gathered a little information. It will be a bit windy, and there will be good bounce. It will be almost similar to England, but there will be a bit more lateral movement.
“Sachin paaji has scored there, so I watched his batting. I watched Dravid sir’s batting. I try to grab knowledge from that and execute whatever is possible for me,” he said.
On missing the Test series in Sri Lanka because of a toe stress fracture, the 24-year-old said: “I wasn’t disappointed because I believe everything good is ahead of us. The last few injuries have been freakish, but because of them, I’ve probably gotten better with my habits and have a better understanding of how to take care of my body... how much I bat and things like that”.

briefs.headline: Knights, Marathas continue to excel
briefs.bodyText:
Kakatiya Knights and Mighty Marathas remained on top of the table with 10 points after registering wins over Rajputana Royals and Chola Chiefs in the Archery Premier League Season 2 at People’s Plaza on Wednesday.

briefs.headline: The bowlers are trying to catch up: New Zealand’s Santner
briefs.bodyText:
It is not often that an exceptionally skilled cricketer like Mitchell Santner hopes and prays for a certain setting instead of banking on his box of tricks.
But such has been the ferocity of India’s T20 batting that the New Zealand white-ball captain wished for surfaces with some assistance for the bowlers in the forthcoming five-match home series.
“We know how good India is. It has power all the way through, as we have seen against the West Indies with high scores and on flat pitches. Hopefully, the pitches are not too flat here because we know what India can do in small grounds,” Santner said during a virtual interaction on Wednesday.
“But if that is the case, we have to find a way to neutralise a powerful attack. We have to turn up, see what is in front of us and adapt as quickly as we can.” The left-arm tweaker, who is a master of subtle variations, spelt out possible tactics to keep the batters in check, but it is easier said than done.
“The only way to stop a team like India is by taking wickets throughout [the innings]. It will be good to take wickets in the PowerPlay even if we go for a few runs. We need to combat the explosive nature of the batters with plans. In the middle overs, we must see if we can go for six singles [in an over] and apply pressure on them,” Santner added.
The 34-year-old stressed that the bowlers were left helpless in the shortest format in this day and age. “The batters have adapted faster while the bowlers are trying to catch up. But with the boundary sizes and flat pitches, there is not much we can do.”
Santner, however, is not one to shy away from a challenge.

briefs.headline: IND vs WI 4th T20I: Hope and Paul sizzle as West Indies trumps India; series drawn at 2-2
briefs.deck: The skipper smashes his second century of the series to power the visiting team to 247 before the seamer derails the host’s chase with a five-for; blistering start by Samson not enough
briefs.bodyText:
It arrived dressed as a stranger, this refreshed pitch at the Rajiv Gandhi International Stadium, with the promise of a different story. India, squinting into the unknown, chose to chase. But the night peeled back the disguise soon enough, and beneath it lay that same old batting paradise.
Shai Hope’s sensational unbeaten century lit the fuse for West Indies’ 24-run win over India on Wednesday, dragging the series level at 2-2.
Jewel Andrew, having taken the pitch’s measure, got to work for the Windies, raining down on Arshdeep Singh with two boundaries and a six that sailed high over mid-wicket.
Mayank Yadav’s pace and bounce backfired, costing him 11 extras.
The visitor tore past 50 in just 15 balls. After Andrew fell to Axar Patel, Shai Hope and Shimron Hetmyer ensured the respite was brief. The Windies registered 79 in the PowerPlay, the joint-highest score in this phase (with New Zealand in Thiruvananthapuram earlier this year) against India in T20Is.
The team 100 came in just 42 balls with India reduced to a hapless spectator.
Hope then found a cautious partner in Rovman Powell, who then burst free to help plunder Axar for 22 runs in an over.
Sherfane Rutherford then joined Hope to stitch together a 91-run stand off just 43 balls, Hope raising his arms to celebrate a ton for the second time in the T20I leg.
Sanju Samson loves Hyderabad and his affection shone bright as he clobbered his way to his joint-fastest T20I fifty off 20 balls, with a daunting 248-run chase before him.
Hope turned to executioner of choice Keemo Paul, who came good not once but twice, first striking Samson off the ledger before sending Ishan Kishan back a few deliveries later.
Abhishek Sharma, who regularly renders his partners obsolete, found himself floundering for rhythm.
As the Sunrisers Hyderabad star dealt with his demons, Shreyas Iyer decided to turn aggressor, injecting life back into the packed stands here at Uppal until an athletic effort from Andrew brought an abrupt end.
Motie’s twin strike
Just when Abhishek began to find the fence, left-arm spinner Gudakesh Motie struck to remove him and Naman Dhir in consecutive balls. The ask: 116 runs from 48 balls.
Tilak Varma and Nitish Kumar’s 32-ball 72 stand lifted hopes high but Paul led the charge with a fifer to dampen any hopes of a win.
Arshdeep retiring hurt was merely the final twist of the knife, hastening a defeat that India tried, in vain, to avoid.

briefs.headline: Hope's ton, Paul's five-for sink India; West Indies level series in Hyderabad
briefs.deck: Paul led the West Indies bowling effort, taking five wickets for 41 runs in his four overs to help seal the win.
briefs.bodyText:
India fell 24 runs short of a target of 248 as the West Indies won the fourth T20I at the Rajiv Gandhi International Stadium in Hyderabad on Wednesday, taking the five-match series to a 2-2 tie.
Sanju Samson gave India a fast start with 56 off 23 balls, but Keemo Paul struck twice in the fifth over to dismiss Samson and Ishan Kishan, denting the chase.
Shreyas Iyer (16 off 11) also fell soon after, before Gudakesh Motie removed Abhishek Sharma (29 off 24) and Naman Dhir (0 off 1) in the 12th over. India were reduced to 130/5 and needed a big partnership to stay in the contest.
Tilak Varma and Nitish Reddy added 70 runs for the sixth wicket to bring India back into the game. Tilak scored 43 off 25 balls, while Reddy made 41 off 20. However, Tilak fell in the 17th over and Reddy was dismissed in the 19th, leaving India with too much to do.
Paul led the West Indies bowling effort, taking five wickets for 41 runs in his four overs to help seal the win.
The series is now level at 2-2, with the fifth and final T20I scheduled to be played in Bengaluru on Saturday, October 17.
Earlier, Shai Hope struck an unbeaten century to help the West Indies post 247/3 after being asked to bat. 
He completed his hundred with a six off the final ball of the innings, finishing on 102 not out off 50 deliveries.
Sherfane Rutherford provided support at the other end, scoring an unbeaten 49 off 26 balls. The pair added 91 runs in 43 balls to push the visitors to a big total.
The West Indies hit 16 sixes and received 18 extras as India's bowlers struggled to contain them. Mayank Yadav and Arshdeep Singh conceded 52 runs each in their four overs, while missed chances in the field also hurt India.
Hope's century was his second of the series, fourth on the tour and third in T20 internationals.

briefs.headline: Karnataka coach Vinay Kumar praises Karun
briefs.bodyText:
For the third straight season, Karnataka has emerged with no more than a point from its Ranji Trophy opener.
But against Andhra on Wednesday in Mulapadu near here, it may not be that bad a result, for it missed all five of its frontline bowlers because of injuries, and handed debuts to three.
If anything, its top-order should have fared better in the first innings, giving a fledgling bowling unit some cushion.
“There were many positives, especially the way the debutants played,” insisted coach R. Vinay Kumar. “Manvanth [Kumar] played a crucial knock in the second innings (44), and Madhav Bajaj also batted well with Karun [Nair].
“The way Karun batted, leading from the front in the second innings, and Smaran’s debut as captain and the composure he showed, were positives.
“In bowling, the lengths could have been much better. But they don’t have much experience. The more they play, they will get better,” the former captain added.
Vinay’s Andhra counterpart Gary Stead was happy with three points.
“Karnataka was last year’s finalist. If you see the 1100-odd runs scored and 33 wickets picked, there was some hard cricket played. We were under a bit of pressure in the final innings and I am proud of the way the boys stood up.”
The former New Zealand coach reserved special praise for S.V. Rahul, 19, and Revanth Reddy, 22, who scored more than half of Andhra’s runs.
“Rahul has a wonderful temperament, and he showed what he can do against a big side like Karnataka, which is great for his development. Revanth can play all three formats, and he’s naturally aggressive. But he also showed a different side of his game. They could both be playing U-23 still, but to be with us is exciting for our future.”

briefs.headline: Abhishek Sharma breaks SKY's record for most sixes in a calendar year
briefs.deck: The Indian opener hit his 69th six of 2026, going past former India captain Suryakumar Yadav's record of 68, which he set in 2022.
briefs.bodyText:
Abhishek Sharma set a new record for the most sixes by a batter representing a full-member nation in T20 internationals in a calendar year during India's fourth T20I against the West Indies in Hyderabad on Wednesday.
The Indian opener hit his 69th six of 2026, going past former India captain Suryakumar Yadav's record of 68, which he set in 2022.
It took Abhishek 15 balls to clear the boundary for the first time in the match, doing so in the ninth over. Sanju Samson had dominated the strike early in the innings, while the West Indies bowlers kept Abhishek's strike rate below 100 after the powerplay.
Abhishek eventually broke free against Shamar Springer, stepping down the track to hit the ball over the boundary.
It has been a mixed but productive year for the left-hander. He started 2026 with 84 off 35 balls against New Zealand in Nagpur, hitting eight sixes, before scoring an unbeaten 68 off just 20 balls, including five sixes, in Guwahati. However, a series of low scores, including five ducks in his first eight innings, slowed his progress.
Earlier in the match, Shai Hope scored an unbeaten century to help the West Indies post 247/3 against India. 
Hope reached his hundred with a six off the final ball of the innings, putting the hosts' bowling attack under pressure.
Hope made 102 not out off 50 balls, while Sherfane Rutherford finished unbeaten on 49 off 26 deliveries. The pair added 91 runs for the fourth wicket in just 43 balls to take the West Indies to a strong total after they were asked to bat.
The visitors hit 16 sixes and received 18 extras as India's bowlers struggled to maintain consistency. Mayank Yadav and Arshdeep Singh conceded 52 runs each in their four overs, while missed chances in the field also hurt the hosts.
Hope's century was his second of the series, fourth on the tour and third in T20 internationals, continuing his strong run of form.
